REQUIREMENT SLUG: namenode-slow-peer-reconfigure
REQUIREMENT FILE: /workspace/requirements/namenode-slow-peer-reconfigure.yaml   <-- READ THIS FIRST

The `title:` field names the real upstream Apache Hadoop JIRA / git commit. Your job is to reproduce that upstream change as faithfully as you can from the requirement text plus the code you find in the tree. Hidden tests derived from the real upstream commit will grade the result, so EXACT naming matters:
  * new/changed configuration keys and their default values (and their entries in *-default.xml)
  * new class / interface / method / field / metric names and their visibility
  * log message wording and format placeholders
  * behavioural details (return values, exception types, ordering, off-by-one boundaries)
If the requirement text names an identifier (class, method, config key, metric, constant), use that identifier verbatim.

HOW TO WORK
1. Read the requirement yaml. Note the JIRA id and the module it belongs to (HDFS / YARN / MAPREDUCE / HADOOP-common / tools).
2. Locate the real code with Grep/Glob. Read enough surrounding code (and the existing tests for it) to make a correct, idiomatic change.
3. Implement the change. Match the surrounding code style, license headers, checkstyle habits (2-space indent, 80-col-ish, final where used, LOG placeholders `{}`).
4. If the change adds a config key, also add it to the matching `*-default.xml` (hdfs-default.xml / core-default.xml / yarn-default.xml / mapred-default.xml) with a sensible description, and to the `DFSConfigKeys`/`YarnConfiguration`/etc. constants class the module uses. Some modules have a TestYarnConfigurationFields / TestHdfsConfigFields style test that requires the xml and the constant to agree - keep them in sync.
5. If the upstream change would have come with tests, add or extend the corresponding test class under the same module (src/test/java/...). Keep tests deterministic and cheap. Do not add tests that need network or a real cluster beyond the usual MiniDFSCluster/MiniYARNCluster idioms already used in that test file.
6. Do NOT run maven/mvn or cmake (there is no warm build environment; it wastes your time). Instead be rigorous by inspection: every symbol you reference must exist (grep to confirm), every new import must be needed and correct, braces/parens balanced, no stale references left behind. Re-read your own final diff (`git diff -- <your files>`) before finishing and fix anything sloppy.
7. Scope discipline: change ONLY what this requirement needs. Do not reformat unrelated lines, do not fix unrelated warnings, do not touch other subsystems. Other agents are concurrently implementing ~380 other requirements in this same working tree.

FORBIDDEN COMMANDS (they would destroy other agents' concurrent work): git checkout / switch / stash / reset / revert / clean / rebase / merge / cherry-pick, `git add -A` or `git add .` without an explicit pathspec, `git commit --amend`, `git rm` of files you did not create, and any `mvn`/`gradle` invocation.

WHEN YOUR IMPLEMENTATION IS COMPLETE - commit it yourself with exactly this shape (substitute the real repo-relative paths you touched, space separated, and keep the flock):

  cd /workspace && flock /tmp/hadoop-git.lock bash -c 'git add -A -- PATH1 PATH2 ... && git diff --cached --binary > requirement_patches/namenode-slow-peer-reconfigure.diff && git commit -q -m "impl: namenode-slow-peer-reconfigure" && git log --oneline -1 && wc -c requirement_patches/namenode-slow-peer-reconfigure.diff'

Rules for that step:
  * List every file you created, modified or deleted as an explicit pathspec. Never a bare directory like `.`.
  * requirement_patches/namenode-slow-peer-reconfigure.diff MUST come out non-empty (wc -c > 0). If `git commit` reports "nothing to commit", another agent already committed your lines: verify the requirement is genuinely satisfied in the working tree, then report that in your notes.
  * Do not touch requirement_patches/ for any other slug.
  * IMPORTANT - a previous interrupted run left some UNCOMMITTED work in this tree. Before you start, run `cd /workspace && git status --short` and inspect `git diff` for the files you expect to touch. If part or all of this requirement is already implemented in the working tree but not yet committed, do NOT redo it from scratch: review it critically, finish/correct anything missing or wrong, then stage exactly those paths and commit as above. That uncommitted work is yours to claim when it belongs to this slug.

FINALLY return ONLY a JSON object (this is your return value, not a message to a human):

title: HDFS-16528. Reconfigure slow peer enable for Namenode
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  NameNode operators may want to turn slow-peer tracking on or off while a cluster is running so they can manage diagnostic overhead without taking the NameNode down. Right now the `dfs.datanode.peer.stats.enabled` setting is not fully reconfigurable on the NameNode side, which makes that operational toggle less useful than related live-reconfig options.


  ## Desired outcome

  The NameNode should allow `dfs.datanode.peer.stats.enabled` to be reconfigured at runtime, with slow-peer tracking behavior updating immediately to match the new boolean value. When disabled, slow-peer reports and JSON output should stop surfacing collected data; when enabled again, the normal slow-peer tracker should resume without requiring a restart.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Administrators can reconfigure `dfs.datanode.peer.stats.enabled` on a live NameNode, the NameNode switches between enabled and disabled slow-peer tracking behavior immediately, disabled mode returns empty slow-peer results instead of stale data, and invalid non-boolean values are rejected as reconfiguration errors rather than being silently accepted.

  '

=== slow-datanode-reconfigurable.yaml
title: HDFS-16287. Support to make dfs.namenode.avoid.read.slow.datanode reconfigurable
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Avoiding slow DataNodes for reads is useful, but NameNode operators need to be able to turn that policy on or off without a restart.


  ## Desired outcome

  `dfs.namenode.avoid.read.slow.datanode` should become a reconfigurable NameNode setting that can be changed at runtime through the standard reconfiguration path.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Live reconfiguration updates the read-avoidance behavior immediately and rejects invalid runtime changes through the normal reconfigure flow.

  '
=== slowpeer-collect-nodes-reconfigurable.yaml
title: HDFS-16327. Make dfs.namenode.max.slowpeer.collect.nodes reconfigurable
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  NameNode operators may need to adjust how many slow peers are retained for reporting without scheduling a restart. Today dfs.namenode.max.slowpeer.collect.nodes behaves like a static setting, which makes live tuning awkward.


  ## Desired outcome

  Make dfs.namenode.max.slowpeer.collect.nodes live-reconfigurable on the NameNode and expose it through the standard reconfigurable-properties listing. Valid changes should take effect immediately in DatanodeManager.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Administrators can reconfigure dfs.namenode.max.slowpeer.collect.nodes at runtime, observe the updated value through the running NameNode, and see the property listed among the NameNode''s reconfigurable settings.

  '
=== slow-peer-jmx-reconfig.yaml
title: HDFS-16634. Dynamically adjust slow peer report size on JMX metrics
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  On busy HDFS clusters, administrators may need to increase or decrease the size of the slow peer report without restarting the NameNode, especially when cluster conditions change during an incident.


  ## Desired outcome

  `dfs.datanode.max.nodes.to.report` should be live reconfigurable so the updated limit immediately controls the slow peer report and also appears in the NameNode''s reconfigurable-properties listing.


  ## Acceptance signals

  After live reconfiguration, the slow peer report expands or contracts without a restart, and administrative tooling shows `dfs.datanode.max.nodes.to.report` among the settings that can be reconfigured at runtime.

  '
